text:
An artistic concept honoring Quechua traditions could center on a visual narrative titled "Breath of the Andes." This piece would feature a protagonist standing at the edge of a terraced mountain landscape, their hands gently resting on the soil to symbolize a deep, spiritual connection with Pachamama (Mother Earth). The artwork would blend the stark, majestic beauty of the Andes peaks with intimate scenes of daily life, such as weaving traditional textiles or tending to crops, highlighting the resilience and harmony inherent in Quechua culture. The color palette would utilize earthy tones—ochre, terracotta, and deep greens—contrasted with the bright blues of the high-altitude sky, reflecting both the struggle and the profound beauty of existence in this region.

Regarding the priority question: The meal that comes second in the day, after breakfast, is lunch.
